content.user_title: Audit Web Accessibility for WCAG Compliance
content.value_statement: Accessibility defects exclude users and create compliance risk. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code review interfaces against WCAG, ARIA, keyboard, and screen reader expectations.
actual_capabilities: Explains WCAG POUR principles and Level AA or AAA checks.
Reviews alt text, color contrast, semantic HTML, form labels, and keyboard access.
Provides accessible patterns for landmarks, dialogs, skip links, live regions, accordions, and tabs.
Lists manual and automated testing steps for common accessibility tools.
Drafts accessibility statement content and known issue sections.
limitations: Does not run automated scanners or inspect a live website by itself.
Does not certify legal compliance with ADA, Section 508, or regional laws.
Examples target WCAG 2.1 and may need updates for newer standards.
Screen reader results still require testing with real assistive technology.

use_cases.title: Fix UI Accessibility Defects
use_cases.description: Review components for labels, focus order, contrast, keyboard support, and semantic structure before release.

use_cases.title: Review Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Check interface plans for accessible names, visual contrast, error states, and inclusive interaction patterns.

use_cases.title: Prepare Audit Evidence
use_cases.description: Build a practical checklist for WCAG, screen reader, keyboard, zoom, and form validation testing.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Page Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one page or screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this page for WCAG 2.1 AA issues. Focus on alt text, headings, labels, contrast, and keyboard access: [page details].

prompt_templates.title: Component Accessibility Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a single UI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this component for accessible names, focus behavior, ARIA use, and keyboard operation. Suggest specific WCAG AA improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Manual Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Planning checks for a user workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a manual accessibility test plan for this workflow. Include keyboard, screen reader, zoom, contrast, and error announcement checks.

prompt_templates.title: Release Audit Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this release as an accessibility reviewer. Rank issues by user impact, cite WCAG areas, and propose acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Audit a product detail page before launch.
output: Missing alt text on product images blocks nonvisual product comparison.
Color contrast on sale pricing appears below WCAG AA for normal text.
Quantity controls need keyboard operation and clear accessible names.

output_examples.input: Assess a checkout modal for keyboard and screen reader support.
output: Move focus into the dialog when it opens and restore focus when it closes.
Add a clear dialog title and description for assistive technology.
Confirm Escape, Tab, Shift Tab, and submit behavior through manual testing.

output_examples.input: Create an accessibility test checklist for a marketing site.
output: Run automated scans with axe, WAVE, Lighthouse, and HTML validation.
Manually test keyboard navigation, zoom at 200 percent, and screen reader landmarks.
Document known issues, owners, severity, and planned remediation dates.

best_practices: Pair automated scans with manual keyboard and screen reader testing.
Use native HTML elements before adding ARIA roles or attributes.
Document issue severity, user impact, WCAG area, owner, and fix status.
anti_patterns: Treating a passing automated scan as full accessibility compliance.
Replacing visible labels with placeholders or hidden names without user need.
Adding ARIA to nonsemantic elements when native controls would work better.

faq.question: Does this skill run accessibility scanners?
faq.answer: No. It gives review guidance and test plans. Use external tools for live scans.

faq.question: Which WCAG version does it cover?
faq.answer: The guidance focuses on WCAG 2.1 Level AA and AAA concepts.

faq.question: Can it replace legal accessibility advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports technical review but does not provide legal certification.

faq.question: Can it help with ARIA implementation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common ARIA states, properties, landmarks, dialogs, live regions, accordions, and tabs.

faq.question: Is manual testing still required?
faq.answer: Yes. Keyboard, screen reader, zoom, and high contrast checks remain necessary.

faq.question: Who benefits from this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, designers, QA teams, and compliance owners can use it during audits and release reviews.
